page: Amazon Web Services i3.16xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Running on the Xen hypervisor, this x86_64 system features 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 488.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.62 GB per core. The hardware includes a massive local storage configuration of 15,200 GB delivered via NVMe SSDs, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance trade-off. Single-core CPU performance is limited, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests consistently scoring in the bottom 10%. However, the 64 vCPUs compensate in multi-threaded workloads, achieving average tier results in multi-core stress-ng, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations remains in the middle 50%, as do Passmark CPU and database operation scores.

Given the high density of local NVMe SSD storage relative to CPU compute, this server is designed for storage-intensive workloads rather than raw single-threaded processing. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high-capacity storage class where resource density favors massive local I/O operations. It is suited for large-scale database deployments, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and distributed file systems where local storage capacity and multi-threaded throughput are prioritized over high single-core clock speeds.
